findings.observation: The complete mace remains inside the canvas, but its top cap begins only about 6% below the top edge, violating the required 8% safe margin.
Exactly one complete mace is shown, with one flanged head, one continuous shaft and grip, and one pommel; no duplicate or separate prop appears.
The compact radial striking flanges, reinforced neck, straight one-hand haft, wrapped grip, and terminal pommel read immediately as a practical flanged mace.

The flanges form a coherent reinforced head around a central socket, the steel shaft is collared at stress points, and the leather-wrapped lower grip and flared pommel support plausible retention and weight.
Worn dark steel dominates the head, neck, shaft, collars, and pommel; the small neutral leather grip wrap remains subordinate and does not imply another rank.
Forged planar flanges with bright abraded steel edges and a subtly hammered, scratched shaft surface establish steel through construction and material response beyond colour alone.
The Standard rank-D mace has no supernatural emission or full-object glow; its narrow blue and warm edge accents are reflected studio light.
The image uses a premium realistic painterly dark-fantasy finish, honest dents and scratches, cold key light with restrained warm rim, and a midnight-charcoal floor and background.

Inspection found no transferred person, clothing, hammer, or design; no published-character resemblance, rarity rainbow, gold inflation, object glow, oversized silhouette, ornament-dependent material identity, extra gear, text, labels, UI, border, frame, logo, or watermark.
